answer: A farm running 179 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the pigment stake is held until the terrace settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the marble audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 45% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. That is 20 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
